title: Mara and the Verdict
premise: Zephyrine Vasquez, archivist of Saltmere Cathedral, is hired by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder listed in the town's oldest ledger has not yet occurred — the victim being a woman who is still alive. As she cross-references fifteen years of meticulously filed secrets, she discovers the ledger's entries are written in advance, and every predicted death has come true on schedule. The trail leads to her own predecessor's locked crypt and a family inheritance built on scheduled sacrifice. In the end Zephyrine must falsify the one record she swore never to alter, breaking the ledger's cycle at the cost of the man she loves — or let the tide take its final entry: herself.
about_author: Lior Voss is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing coastal archives before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about paper trails that outlive the people they describe.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A pale stranger named Corwin Hale pays triple rate to verify that 'E. Marsh' was not murdered in 1911 — insisting the entry must be proven false before it happens. The emotional beat is professional unease curdling into fascination as she takes money she shouldn't.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She searches her immaculate archive for E. Marsh and finds the ledger page torn out — but the stub remains, dated next month. The beat is quiet dread: her ordered world has a hole shaped like a future.

chapters.title: Edith Marsh, Alive
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She tracks down Edith Marsh, ninety-one and sharp-tongued, living above the chandlery. Edith recognizes the ledger description instantly and goes white. The beat is the first crack in the town's polite silence.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Filing
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Zephyrine's POV. How she came to Saltmere after her father's disgrace, and how the previous archivist, Father Ambrose, taught her that records are promises. Ends with his sudden death and the crypt he sealed. Beat: grief disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Corwin's Contradictions
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Corwin claims to be a genealogist, but his questions are all about dates of death, not birth. She notices salt water stains on his cuffs though he says he can't swim. Beat: suspicion sharpening into attraction she resents.

chapters.title: The Tide Tables
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She overlays the ledger's death dates with tide charts: every entry coincides with an extreme spring tide. The next one falls in nineteen days. Beat: cold arithmetic replacing fear with method.

chapters.title: What the Warden Saw
chapters.summary: Warden Ilsa Brandt's POV. The cathedral warden recalls Ambrose descending into the crypt the week he died, carrying a box. She lied to the coroner then; she won't say why now. Beat: guilt as a locked door.

chapters.title: Entry 1911
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Reconstructing the torn page from ink impressions on the sheet beneath it: 'E. Marsh — taken by the tide, debt paid.' But Edith Marsh is alive, which means either the ledger failed once — or the name means someone else. Beat: hope with a trapdoor under it.

chapters.title: The Chandlery Fire
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Edith's home burns overnight; Edith survives because she'd left to sleep at her daughter's. Arson, clearly meant for the old woman. Beat: the ledger doesn't predict deaths — it schedules them.

chapters.title: Corwin Confesses Half
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Corwin admits he isn't a genealogist: his grandmother was the original E. Marsh's sister, and the family has paid 'the cathedral debt' for generations. He hired Zephyrine hoping a neutral archivist could break the pattern. Beat: trust offered too late to be clean.

chapters.title: The Debt Explained
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. His family history: in 1911, the Marshes' shipping fortune was saved from ruin by a bargain struck with the cathedral's founders — one life per generation, entered in advance, 'paid by the tide.' Beat: inherited horror, told flatly, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Marginalia
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She decodes Father Ambrose's pencil marks in the surviving ledgers: tiny crosses beside entries where he intervened. Three lives were saved. Three other names died instead. Beat: her mentor was both protector and accomplice.

chapters.title: Ilsa Breaks
chapters.summary: Warden Brandt's POV. Confronted with Ambrose's marginalia, Ilsa admits she helped him seal the crypt — Ambrose found the founders' original covenant inside and wanted it buried with himself. Beat: loyalty revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: Down into the Crypt
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. With Ilsa's key, Zephyrine enters the flooded lower crypt at low tide and finds Ambrose's box: the founding covenant, a second ledger, and a photograph of her own father. Beat: vertigo — the mystery just swallowed her past.

chapters.title: My Father's Signature
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Her disgraced father was the last signatory of the covenant; his 'disgrace' was refusing to enter the current generation's name. Someone else signed for him. Beat: betrayal reframing everything she filed away about her childhood.

chapters.title: Who Signed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Handwriting analysis against her own archive: the signature matching her father's line belongs to the current cathedral dean, Dean Osgood Pell — the man who gave her the job. Beat: the ground tilting beneath institutional trust.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Dean
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A tense supper where Pell speaks warmly about legacy, tides, and 'what the town owes.' He knows she's been in the crypt; he says so with a smile. Beat: menace wearing vestments.

chapters.title: The Empty Entry
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The second ledger's newest page holds this generation's entry — name blank, date filled: the spring tide, nineteen days out. The blank is a vacancy waiting to be filled. Beat: countdown begins in earnest.

chapters.title: Corwin Vanishes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Corwin misses their meeting; his hotel room is stripped, a tide table circled on the desk. Either he fled or was taken. Beat: loneliness sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Edith's Testimony
chapters.summary: Edith Marsh's POV. The old woman finally tells all: she was the intended victim sixty years ago until Ambrose substituted another name — a drifter no one missed. She has lived as 'debt paid' ever since, and it hollowed her. Beat: survival as its own sentence.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Edith's POV continues. Edith warns Zephyrine: breaking the cycle killed the last person who tried — a young deacon in 1963, drowned on a calm day. 'The tide keeps accounts.' Beat: warning delivered with terrible tenderness.

chapters.title: Archive Under Watch
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She returns to find her office searched, files subtly reordered — someone using her own system against her. She sets a hair-trap and dust test. Beat: the hunter becoming the hunted in her own territory.

chapters.title: Caught in the Act
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The trap springs: it's Corwin, alive, sneaking back for the covenant. His flight wasn't cowardice — Pell summoned him and offered to erase the Marsh debt if Corwin delivered the documents. Beat: relief and fury entangled.

chapters.title: A Deal with the Dean
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. Flashback to Pell's offer: betray the archive, save his bloodline, let the blank entry be filled with anyone. Corwin refused — but didn't report it. Beat: shame confessed, love admitted in the same breath.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Corwin, alternating short scenes. They admit what's growing between them while planning to steal the covenant and expose Pell. Each privately calculates whether the other is the tide's likeliest target. Beat: tenderness shadowed by arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Founders' Covenant
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Full reading of the covenant: the 'debt' was invented by the founding families to launder a murder-for-inheritance scheme in 1911 — the ledger is a forgery sustained by belief and murder. Beat: the supernatural collapsing into something more human and worse.

chapters.title: But the Dates Hold
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. If it's a forgery, why do the predictions keep coming true? She realizes the answer: whoever holds the ledger makes them true. It's not prophecy — it's a murder rota passed between deans. Beat: horror relocating from the occult to the office.

chapters.title: Pell's Predecessor
chapters.summary: Ilsa Brandt's POV. Ilsa reveals Pell's mentor drowned mysteriously in 1998 — right after trying to end the practice. Pell didn't inherit a sacred duty; he inherited a weapon and a habit. Beat: the institution eating its own.

chapters.title: Setting the Trap
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Plan: forge a completed entry naming Pell himself, plant it in the second ledger, and let his superstition do the rest. Corwin objects — it makes them murderers of a sort. Beat: moral cost priced out loud.

chapters.title: The Forged Page
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She commits the one act she swore never to commit: falsifying a record. The craftsmanship is perfect; her hands shake anyway. Beat: transgression as character climax — the archivist unmaking her own creed.

chapters.title: Pell Takes the Bait
chapters.summary: Dean Pell's POV. Pell finds the entry, and terror cracks his certainty. He moves the spring tide vigil forward, summons the wardens, prepares to flee with the ledgers. Beat: predator discovering it is also prey.

chapters.title: Night Vigil
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The cathedral on the eve of the spring tide: candles, wardens, Pell clutching the ledgers, Zephyrine and Corwin hidden in the archive gallery. Beat: held breath across the whole building.

chapters.title: The Tide Turns Early
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Pell, spooked, tries to burn the ledgers rather than face the entry — destroying the evidence with them. Zephyrine intervenes; struggle on the flooded crypt stairs. Beat: chaos where control used to be.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The extreme tide floods the lower crypt and dislodges Ambrose's sealed chamber, revealing the 1963 deacon's remains — and Pell's mentor's confession letter, waterproofed in lead. Beat: the sea testifying at last.

chapters.title: Confession in the Water
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Cornered by rising water and the confession letter naming him, Pell breaks — half repentance, half rage — and nearly pulls Zephyrine under with him. Corwin saves her; Pell is taken by the undertow. Beat: the ledger's last entry writing itself.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Pell's body is recovered at dawn; officially an accident during a storm vigil. Zephyrine holds the real evidence and must decide what the record will say. Beat: power over truth, felt as a weight.

chapters.title: The Honest Ledger
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She writes the true account — the murders, the covenant, the names — and seals it to open in fifty years, protecting the living town while refusing to lie. Beat: integrity redefined rather than abandoned.

chapters.title: Edith's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Edith Marsh's POV. Edith, freed at last from 'debt paid,' chooses to sign her own name in the archive's public register — the first time in sixty years her existence is recorded without condition. Beat: quiet, earned grace.

chapters.title: What Remains Filed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Weeks later: the archive restored, Corwin staying in Saltmere, their relationship tentative and real. She reorganizes nothing; some disorder is honest. Beat: healing without forgetting.

chapters.title: Mara and the Verdict
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Zephyrine's POV. On the anniversary tide, she reads her father's old letter — revealing her childhood nickname, Mara, and his plea that she judge the town gently. She closes the ledger, locks the crypt, and lets the sea keep its silence. Beat: verdict rendered, mercy included.
